subject: Any other license better support commercial use case?

messages.author: 6e1fdac61783d2b3
messages.subject: Any other license better support commercial use case?
parts:
Dear Renjin contributors:

I wonder beside GPL3, is there any other more commercial friendly license we can use? Currently we are exploring Renjin on spark and hope to use it for commercial production use cases.

Thanks!

Kang

messages.author: 3b104dc6686d0c85
messages.subject: Re: Any other license better support commercial use case?
parts:
Hi Kang,

this is a frequently asked question and the short answer is "no", but software licenses are a complicated business. Here's a previous discussion on the support group: https://groups.google.com/d/msg/renjin-dev/yoS1dTeJLm8/bVtVu_tGLck​ which may help you understand why Renjin is GPLv3 licensed.

Let us know if you have more questions or give us some more details about how you intend to use Renjin so we can better understand the implications from a licensing point of view.

Maarten-Jan

messages.author: 6e1fdac61783d2b3
messages.subject: Re: Any other license better support commercial use case?
parts:
Hi Maarten,

Thanks for the quick reply. I see why Renjin want to use GPL. I used to work for big companies. My feeling is that GPLv3 might very strict but GPLv2 is "OK". Is it possible to use Renjin under GPLv2?

Thanks

Kang

messages.author: f06db63329fab1f9
messages.subject: Re: Any other license better support commercial use case?
parts:
Hi Kang,
Could you tell me a little more about what you see as problematic differences between GPLv3 and v2? I believe the choice to license Renjin under v3 was primarily driven at the time by the fact that v3 was the "latest" version of the GPL at the time of Renjin's inception.

Relicensing Renjin under GPLv2 would require tracking down our various contributors and obtaining their permission, so I think we would need to have a specific, compelling reason to do so.

Best,
Alex

messages.author: 6e1fdac61783d2b3
messages.subject: Re: Any other license better support commercial use case?
parts:
Hi Alex,

Thanks for the reply. I don't know the detail difference between v2 and v3 (Sth found here: http://stackoverflow.com/questions/41460/what-are-the-differences-between-gpl-v2-and-gpl-v3-licenses). and I'll look into it further. What I know know is GPLv3 is more restrict than v2 and industrial people don't like v3 much. I have this feeling because I used to work in Amazon and now in Apple, both of them don't like v3 (prohibit use in production). And v2 is on the boundary, kind of OK. For example, we are allowed to use old version of some other machine learning library.

R is one of the two widely used data scientist language in industry (another one is python). The advantage of R is it have better statistics support. However, integrating R into the mainstream JVM based solution is a pain because of all kinds of dependency problems. Most of of large industry company like amazon, twitter, google, apple use java dominately. Renjin is a great solution for industry because it is fully JVM implementation. I hope to integrate it with Apache Spark so we can parallel train and predict the model. I didn't find better solution to build statistics model on top of JVM than Renjin.

Currently I am experimenting on integrating Renjin and spark (there are also one open source project like https://github.com/onetapbeyond/renjin-spark-executor). If we can make use of Renjin (with a relative soft license) in our data pipeline, that would enable us to build better things.

Thanks

Kang
